details: US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum exchange-traded funds have recorded over $1 billion in combined net outflows in October through October 8, with numbers exceeding $1.29 billion across all crypto funds by October 10. Bitcoin ETFs experienced significant losses of $678.9 million between October 7 and October 10, while Ethereum ETFs noted nine consecutive days of outflows. This trend suggests a reduction of risk exposure by institutional investors.
title: US Crypto ETFs See Over $1 Billion in October Outflows

details: Bitcoin has rebounded to approximately $82,500 after previously dipping to $80,427, but its upward momentum faces challenges from rising US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar, and general financial market volatility. This environment is contributing to capital shifting towards alternative, perceived as more stable, assets.
sourceName: KuCoin (referencing Farside Investors and CoinGecko data)
title: Bitcoin Recovers Above $82,500 Amid Persistent Macro Headwinds

details: A year after the significant "10/10 crash" of October 10, 2025, Bitcoin and Ether have largely restored their market liquidity, significantly supported by ETF inflows and institutional buying. In contrast, altcoins have not demonstrated the same recovery in liquidity or rally lengths, indicating a "two-speed market" where Bitcoin and Ether are increasingly behaving like institutional assets.
title: Bitcoin and Ether Liquidity Rebounds While Altcoins Lag

details: The U.S. government moved 12,267 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.01 billion and linked to the 2016 Bitfinex hack, to new, unlabeled addresses on October 8. Additionally, around $770 million in other seized Bitcoin reached Coinbase Prime between October 6 and 7. These transfers are being monitored by traders for potential selling pressure, though the absence of immediate deposits to exchanges suggests no confirmed plans for an imminent sale.
title: US Government Moves Over $1 Billion in Bitfinex-Seized Bitcoin
